title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-02-27
lineage: SBD 16-Track Master Reel > Rough Mix DAT > DATx3 > Digital Sound Card > WAV > SHN > WAV > Cool Edit > CDWAV > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording captures a legendary ’69 show highlighted by a cosmic Dark Star and flawless St. Stephen, with crystal‑clear mix and soaring band performance.
ai_review.review: The gd69‑02‑27.sbd tape delivers an outstanding soundboard capture – crisp, open, and balanced – that lets listeners hear every nuance of the band’s fire‑breathing 1969 set.  The show shines on the Mountains of the Moon → Dark Star transition, a blistering Eleven, luminous Lovelight, and a monster Other One suite, all bolstered by Jerry’s soaring solos, Phil’s thunderous bass, and tight drumming.  Fans rave about the first‑set banter and the second‑set’s epic flow, making this recording a must‑have for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 detailed 5‑star reviews praise both performance and audio quality; the show is repeatedly called one of the best ’69 performances, and the soundboard source is described as crystal clear.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners note an open, crisp mix with better separation than the Live/Dead release; no drop‑outs or muddiness reported. Bobby’s drums are slightly forward in the mix, adding presence.

standout_songs: Mountains of the Moon → Dark Star
Cryptical Envelopment > The Other One > Cryptical Reprise
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds with playful banter and tight jams; second set delivers a seamless Dark Star transition, a scorching Eleven, and an epic Other One suite, keeping the momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as having perfect tone, soaring leads, and an incredible solo in Lovelight; his guitar work is called “cosmic” and “fiery”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for “throwing down the thunder” on The Eleven, providing a powerful bass foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for fluid right‑hand rhythmic fills on Doin' That Rag and overall rhythm guitar contribution.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ interplay with Jerry called stellar; organ work highlighted as a key part of the show’s texture.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bobby (drummer) is higher in the mix than on Live/Dead, with memorable intro banter (“Thumpy & Drumstick”) and tight, driving drumming throughout.
